questions: Have you noticed a shaking or tremor in your hands, especially when they are at rest?
Do you have trouble starting to walk, feeling as if your feet are glued to the floor?
Have you ever been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease?
Have you had a stroke or a brain injury in the past?
Do you have weakness on one side of your body?
Do you have pain in your back or legs when you walk that is relieved by sitting or leaning forward?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your feet or legs?
Do you have a history of diabetes?
Do you have any memory problems or confusion?
orders: MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast
10-meter walk test to measure baseline gait speed and stride length
Timed Up and Go (TUG) test for baseline mobility assessment
Large-volume lumbar puncture (removing 30-50 mL of CSF) as a diagnostic tap test
Repeat 10-meter walk and TUG test 1-2 hours after the lumbar puncture
Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) to objectively screen for cognitive impairment
Post-void bladder scan to measure urinary retention
Cervical and thoracic spine MRI to rule out spinal cord compression as a cause of gait apraxia
results: 1. MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast
